newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico suggests early buyback on Brady bonds.
newsitem.headline: Mexico suggests early buyback on Brady bonds.

text.p: A Mexican official on Wednesday suggested that Mexico bought back outstanding Brady bonds before placing a 20-year $1.0 billion bond issue last week.
Government officials later confirmed that they had purchased Brady bonds, but declined to say whether the purchase took place before the bond placement.
When Mexico announced the new bond issue, it said it was designated specifically to buy back Brady bonds.

Finance Ministry spokesman Alejandro Valenzuela suggested the buyback had occurred when he was asked at a news conference about market speculation that Mexico bought the outstanding Brady bonds before placing the 20-year issue.

"Now, it would be illogical to first place an issue and then to buy them (Brady bonds) because obviously it would affect the price and the discount in the secondary market," Valenzuela said in response to the question,

"It would not be beneficial for the country. These are trades that are often made in the markets in an opportunisitic way, seeking to obtain funds that lessen the country's debt," Valenzuela said in Spanish.

Market analysts said that trading patterns in recent weeks in the Brady market suggest that Mexico bought back some if not all of the $1.24 billion worth of discount Brady bonds that it said it would when it placed the 20-year issue on September 17.

"I believe that in this sense the country fortunately has been successful on the one hand in the capital markets and on the other to succeed in obtaining a discount that is useful in opening room in our budget for other needs," Valenzuela said.
The 20-year issue payed a premium of 445 basis points over U.S. Treasuries.
